title: SpaceXSI Shifts AI Usage to Weekly Pools in Unified X Subscription

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Existing Cursor and Grok users can now merge their accounts into a single billing plan that redistributes AI access into a shared seven day allowance. This new system replaces previous monthly quotas with a weekly usage pool across all integrated tools and removes subsidies for third-party AI models, such as GPT and Claude, which are now billed at provider API list prices. Some users report that these new shared limits are exhausted more quickly than under legacy plans, prompting warnings to avoid switching immediately.

The X Subscription offers four paid tiers: Plus at $8, Premium at $30, Super at $100, and Ultra at $200 per month. Paid members receive at least double the coding usage on Grok models compared to equivalent standalone Cursor plans. The transition is optional, and those who opt in receive prorated refunds for unused time on eligible monthly and annual plans. Cursor Pro and Pro+ subscribers are offered discounted transition rates of $20 for Premium or $60 for Super for six months.

selectedTweets.text:
One plan now covers Cursor, Grok, Grok Bot, and X.

This is the biggest change to how Cursor is priced.

If you've been with us since the early days, this will feel like a lot, so I'll walk you through it.

First, every change is opt-in. If you do nothing, nothing happens.

You can keep your current plan with the same benefits, behavior, and pricing, and still move between the current plans. New sign-ups and anyone upgrading from free Cursor go to the new plans.

Here's what's different:

1. First-party usage

For most users, Grok and Composer coding limits are at least double what the matching Cursor plan gives you today.

We worked hard to make usage grow faster than price at each tier:

Plus ($8/mo): our base plan
Premium ($30/mo): 4x Plus usage
Super ($100/mo): 15x Plus usage
Ultra ($200/mo): 50x Plus usage

That's on top of every other product included in the plan.

On the new plans, Cursor usage limits move from monthly to weekly. Grok, Cursor, and X share one weekly pool.

All Grok Bot usage is treated as first-party. So on Premium and up, you get at least double the Grok Bot usage.

We know AI can get expensive. If you're trusting us, you should get as much as we can deliver. That's what we're aiming for with these new plans.

2. Products

Every paid plan includes X Premium features. Grok @Bot comes with Premium and up.

If you're reading this on X, you can now get those features as part of Cursor and @Grok. Your plan also covers Grok chat, Voice, and Imagine images and video.

Grok Bot access has been one of the biggest pain points we've heard since it launched, and it's a big part of why we're excited.

3. Third-party models

You can keep using every model you rely on in Cursor.

What's changing is how those models are billed on the new plans: they come out of your usage credits at the provider's API list price, the same as paying the provider directly.

Current Cursor plans subsidize third-party models, so you can get inference below API price.

At @spacexai, we want to give you as much value as we can on our own models. That's why Grok usage limits are increasing and why we're treating Grok Bot usage as first-party.

We're still committed to Cursor being the simplest way to use models from many providers in one place, and we'll have more news on this front in the coming weeks.

If most of your usage is on third-party models, the new plans might cost you more, so check your usage before switching. That's one of the main reasons these plans are opt-in.

Cursor Pro and Pro+ subscribers who switch get Premium at $20/mo or Super at $60/mo for 6 months (normally $30 and $100).

4. Credit unification

Cursor credits and xAI API credits are coming together - prepaid xAI API balances now move into Cursor.

If you've been running the xAI API and Cursor as separate accounts, this is the start of managing both in one place.

It also means tools like Grok Voice become more accessible to all builders, and our biggest Grok users can now take full advantage of Cursor.

That's a lot of stuff! In summary:

Cursor, Grok, and X are all part of SpaceXSI.

That gives us economies of scale, and this unification is one of the main ways we can pass that on to you as savings and more usage.

Whether you should switch depends on which products you use, and that's different for everyone. If you pay for X today or most of your usage is on Grok, the new plans are probably a better deal.

To get started, check out https://t.co/X0mYoAxcru

What hasn't changed is why we do this: we want to build the best tools we can for you, and we think one plan across all of these products gets us closer to that.

If something here doesn't make sense or feels unfair, please let me know. I'm here to help.

selectedTweets.bestBit: eligible monthly and annual plans are cancelled, and you get a prorated refund for unused time
selectedTweets.text:
If you have an existing Cursor, Grok, and or 𝕏 subscription, here's how to unify/combine all your accounts into the new 𝕏 Subscription:

When you switch from your current plan, eligible monthly and annual plans are cancelled, and you get a prorated refund for unused time. The refund goes back to your original payment method separately from your checkout total, so your new plan is charged at full price.

If you pay for Cursor through the Apple App Store, switching doesn't cancel that subscription, and 𝕏 can't refund it. Cancel it in your iPhone or iPad Settings so Apple stops billing you, and request any refund from Apple.

Switching is optional. If you don’t switch, your current plan continues unless you change or cancel it.

Existing Cursor, Grok, or X subscribers can switch to The X Subscription and unify eligible accounts at https://t.co/6ngNvnaUxD (Cursor), https://t.co/TvLTfpUdIa (Grok), or on https://t.co/x2jegk0c1X (X) via the in-product banner. If you already pay for Cursor, Grok, or X, switch on the web at one of these links.

For now, the mobile apps send you to the web to switch. If you don't pay for any of them yet, you can set up a new account and subscribe to The X Subscription in the Grok, X, Grok Bot, or Cursor mobile apps, if desired. These purchases are billed through the App Store or Google Play Store.

Switching unifies eligible Cursor and Grok accounts into one account with one workspace, one plan, and one bill. Adding a personal X account gives you X benefits under The X Subscription. A completed unification is permanent. It can’t be undone, and Support can’t undo it for you. After you unify, you manage your plan, billing, and settings at https://t.co/clftXLxBN7.

When you switch, your old Cursor, Grok, and X Premium subscriptions are cancelled automatically, so you don’t need to cancel them yourself. Any refund for unused time is sent separately.

If your X, Grok, and Cursor accounts use different email addresses, they don’t need to match. 𝕏 will connect the X account you sign in to, not an account that shares your email. When you switch, sign in to the exact Cursor, Grok, and X accounts you want to combine, and check each one before you confirm. Keep work and personal accounts separate unless you mean to combine them. If the wrong account appears, stop before checkout and contact Support.

 Learn more: https://t.co/YwVMMz81bZ

selectedTweets.text:
⚠️ Don't rush to switch to the new X Subscription tiers.

Grok, Imagine, Voice, Bot, and Cursor now share one weekly usage limit. The more you use one, the less you have for the others.

xAI claims more usage-per-dollar but some users are reporting their limits running out much faster than the old plans.

If you're on a legacy plan you might want to keep it for now, or at least wait until more users confirm whether the new plans are actually better.

selectedTweets.text:
Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X subscriptions unified.

I asked Grok to simplify the changes and options:

Cursor, Grok, Grok Bot and X Premium are now one optional plan. Do nothing and your current Cursor plan stays exactly the same (price, limits, everything).

New opt-in tiers:

- Plus $8 – base
- Premium $30 – 4× Plus usage
- Super $100 – 15× Plus
- Ultra $200 – 50× Plus

First-party stuff (Grok, Composer, Grok Bot) is at least double the old matching Cursor limits for most people, and it’s all in one weekly pool. Every paid plan includes full X Premium features. Grok Bot is treated as first-party from Premium up.

Third-party models on the new plans are billed at full API price (no more subsidy).

What you should do

- Mostly use Grok / already pay for X → switch. Better value and more first-party usage.
- Mostly third-party models in Cursor → check your usage first. It might cost you more.
- Happy with your current Cursor plan → stay put. Nothing changes.
- On Cursor Pro/Pro+ → special rate for 6 months if you switch (Premium $20 or Super $60).

Opt-in only.
